subject: Post-call: Crestline POC goals, SLA targets, and token economics (readback)
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Healy <tom.healy@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Crestline POC goals, SLA targets, and token economics (readback)

Tom / Sophie — thanks again for taking time today. Below is a quick readback from our call to lock in the POC scope, success criteria, evaluation plan and owners. Please reply with any corrections; otherwise we’ll treat this as the working plan and kick off the workstreams next week.

High-level objective
- Validate Redwood Inference can serve Crestline’s clinical summarization pipeline at production-like scale while meeting latency & cost targets and maintaining clinical fidelity.

Primary success criteria (measured during 3-week POC) — agreed:
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 300 ms for 512-token prompts (target 250 ms).
- Throughput: sustained 120 inference requests/minute (~2 rps) for the sampled workload with <=5% error rate.
- Token economics: average inference cost <= $0.0014 per token (including batching benefits) measured on Redwood Dedicated dev pool.
- Quality: automated ROUGE-L and clinical-entity-extraction F1 >= 0.86 on Crestline test set + manual review pass rate >= 90% for 40 sampled summaries.

Data & workload
- You will provide: 5k de-identified clinical notes (sample set) + 200 representative long-note examples for stress testing. File: crestline_sample_workload_v2.jsonl (attached).
- Expected average prompt length: 420 tokens, generation length: 220 tokens. Please confirm if tokenization assumptions above are representative.

Evaluation plan and phases
1) Week 0 (prep, target week of Jun 4): onboarding, upload sample dataset to customer-controlled bucket, baseline profiling. Owner: Ben (infra onboarding).
2) Week 1 (Jun 11–17): smoke runs, tuning batch/kv-cache, initial latency/throughput profiling. Owner: Karthik (perf tuning) + Ben.
3) Week 2 (Jun 18–24): quality evaluation vs Crestline test set (automated metrics + manual review), cost modeling. Owner: Marissa (quality eval).
4) Week 3 (Jun 25–30): final run, readout, and playbook for production rollout (if accepted). Owner: Ava (readout & next steps).

Canary and fallback
- Canary model: open-model-variant v2.1 (quantized) with fallback to standard fp16 model if quality regresses >3%.

Deliverables
- Weekly scorecard (latency/throughput/cost/quality).
- Runbook with recommended batching/quant settings and estimated unit economics.
- Final readout deck and go/no-go recommendation.

Immediate asks from Crestline
- Confirm sample file tokenization assumptions and share expected peak concurrency window (time of day / number of parallel users).
- If procurement wants an early overview, loop in procurement@crestlinehealth.com and we’ll supply an SOW template.

Attachments: crestline_poc_mop_v1.pdf (POC scope + SOW template), crestline_sample_workload_v2.jsonl (sample records).

Next step: Ben will reach out to provision Dev Dedicated pool and share access; Karthik will post initial profiling plan by EOD Monday. If no corrections from you, we’ll schedule a kickoff for Tue Jun 5 at 10:00 PT.

Thanks — Ava
Ava Chen | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0186
From: Tom Healy <tom.healy@crestlinehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@crestlinehealth.com>, procurement@crestlinehealth.com
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Crestline POC goals, SLA targets, and token economics (readback)

Ava — thanks for the clear readback. A few clarifications and small edits from our side:
- Latency: 300 ms P95 acceptable as a hard SLO for the POC. We can agree to the tighter target (250 ms) as a stretch goal.
- Throughput: the 120 req/min is for the night-batch processing window; peak interactive load during day is ~15 concurrent users (expected burst ~40 concurrent requests over 60s). Please ensure the plan tests both patterns.
- Token economics: procurement will want a conservative cost estimate that assumes worst-case (no batching) for their initial budget planning. Suggest we provide both "batching realistic" and "worst-case" numbers in the cost model.
- Quality: 40 manual samples is fine. For automated checks we’ll add a clinical entity recall threshold (we propose recall >= 0.88).

One ask: we have some notes that cannot leave our VPC for the trial. Can Redwood run the Dedicated dev pool in our VPC or provide an on-prem connector? Sophie will follow up on technical constraints.

Tom
Tom Healy | VP, Clinical Products
Crestline Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Healy <tom.healy@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Crestline POC goals, SLA targets, and token economics (readback)

Adding implementation notes and owner confirmations.
- VPC/on-prem: Ben to coordinate with Infra (I’ll open a ticket with infra-ops) to confirm we can provision a Dedicated dev pool in Crestline VPC or provide a secure connector by Wed Jun 6.
- Profiling plan: I’ll run both patterns Tom asked for — (a) night-batch 120 req/min sustained run, (b) daytime burst test 40 concurrent requests over 60s. I’ll include worst-case (no batching) and realistic-batching cost curves in the Week 1 report.
- Tokenization: Karthik — please validate tokenization assumptions against the sample file and share a short summary (median prompt tokens, generation tokens) by Wed Jun 6.
- Manual review: Marissa will coordinate with Tom to pick the 40 records and set up the rubric + Slack channel for quick feedback.

Action items (owners):
- Infra/provisioning (Ben) — ticket created, target Wed Jun 6.
- Tokenization & perf knobs (Karthik) — summary by Wed Jun 6.
- Quality rubric & manual review logistics (Marissa) — confirm reviewers and rubric by Jun 8.
- Kickoff scheduling (Ava) — confirm Tue Jun 5 10:00 PT; Tom please confirm.

I’ll post the infra ticket link as soon as it’s created.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
